note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 104, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: The 11 August 1796 engagement is Moreau’s Army of the Rhine and Moselle against the Austrian field army under Archduke Charles. Local forces preserve this historical command scope without using a present-day Austrian or French state identity. These sources review event and force identity; CDB numerical estimates and uncertainty are retained, not independently certified. Identity review (attacker; original CDB90 name AUS ARMY): Sources identify this local battlefield force. The display name clarifies the original CDB designation; its numerical estimates and uncertainty are unchanged. Identity review (defender; original CDB90 name FR ARMY OF THE RHINE AND MOSELLE): Sources identify this local battlefield force. The display name clarifies the original CDB designation; its numerical estimates and uncertainty are unchanged.

Equipment review: the source-named FR ARMY OF THE RHINE AND MOSELLE retains its complete CDB90 aggregate and all strength and loss estimates. A cocked-hat infantryman with a Model 1777-style flintlock and socket bayonet illustrates one documented French infantry equipment component. Contemporary dress and weapons varied; the model does not establish the uniform, firearm type or troop composition of every soldier, nor represent cavalry, artillery or attached contingents. Identity evidence is recorded separately from the museum equipment sources. The assignment uses the 1792–1803 Republican profile; no shako is introduced before 1806.
